name: Ventilation Solutions for Windowless Los Angeles Bathroom Remodels

mainEntity.name: How can I remodel a small Los Angeles bathroom to meet current ventilation and moisture code without adding an exterior window?
mainEntity.text: How can I remodel a small Los Angeles bathroom to meet current ventilation and moisture code without adding an exterior window?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many Los Angeles bathrooms lack exterior walls or windows, and most online advice glosses over how to achieve code-compliant ventilation in these interior spaces. You generally do not need to add a window if you provide mechanical ventilation that meets current code requirements. First, calculate the required fan capacity in cubic feet per minute (CFM) based on bathroom size and fixtures; undersized fans are a common failure point. Choose a quiet, ducted exhaust fan and vent it all the way outdoors—typically through the roof or an exterior wall—not into an attic or crawl space, which can cause moisture damage and mold. Use smooth metal ducting, keep runs as short and straight as possible, and properly insulate and seal the duct to reduce condensation and air leakage. For small interior Los Angeles bathrooms, a humidity-sensing or timer-controlled fan is often the easiest way to ensure adequate run time after showers. Combine this with mold-resistant drywall, tile backer, proper waterproofing in wet zones, and careful sealing around penetrations. During planning, have your contractor confirm local mechanical code requirements and coordinate with the roofing contractor for roof penetrations, flashing, and warranties, so your new ventilation solution is both compliant and watertight.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use a correctly sized, ducted exhaust fan vented to the exterior, often through the roof, with a timer or humidity sensor. Meet minimum CFM based on room size, use smooth metal ducting with minimal bends, and seal penetrations. Combined with mold-resistant materials, this satisfies ventilation without adding a window.
